proof_nl:
Fix an integer n>1, a real number x, and an integer z. We will show that E(n,x+z)=E(n,x).

By definition,
E(n,x+z)=\lfloor n(x+z)\rfloor-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor k(x+z)\rfloor}{k}.
For each integer k with 1\le k\le n, both nz and kz are integers. Using the standard floor translation identity \lfloor t+m\rfloor=\lfloor t\rfloor+m for every real t and integer m, we get
\lfloor n(x+z)\rfloor=\lfloor nx+nz\rfloor=\lfloor nx\rfloor+nz,
and similarly
\lfloor k(x+z)\rfloor=\lfloor kx+kz\rfloor=\lfloor kx\rfloor+kz.
Substituting these into the definition of E(n,x+z) gives
E(n,x+z)=\bigl(\lfloor nx\rfloor+nz\bigr)-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor+kz}{k}.
Distributing the sum,
E(n,x+z)=\lfloor nx\rfloor+nz-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor}{k}-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{kz}{k}.
Since \frac{kz}{k}=z for each k, the last sum equals \sum_{k=1}^n z=nz. Therefore the added nz terms cancel:
E(n,x+z)=\lfloor nx\rfloor-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor}{k}=E(n,x).
Hence E(n,x+z)=E(n,x) for every real x and every integer z.
solver_summary: Apply the floor translation identity to nx and each kx after adding the integer shift z; the resulting nz terms cancel in the definition of E(n,x).
vetter_reason: The proof correctly establishes translation invariance under integer shifts: floor(t+m)=floor(t)+m is applied appropriately to both terms, and the added nz terms cancel exactly in the sum. The lemma matches the assembly role and does not drift from the root objective structure.
